title: Trionic Array II
summary: Given an integer array of length n, identify the longest contiguous subarray where the elements first strictly increase, then strictly decrease, and finally strictly increase again.
statement: Given an integer array of length n, identify the longest contiguous subarray where the elements first strictly increase, then strictly decrease, and finally strictly increase again. Return the sum of this subarray with the highest possible sum.
constraints: The array has at least four signed integers.
A valid subarray has nonempty strictly increasing, decreasing, then increasing edge runs.
Return the maximum sum among all valid contiguous subarrays.
hints: Track the best sum ending at each of the four pattern phases.
Update single, first increase, decrease, and final increase states from the previous index.
Strictly rising edges advance or extend increasing states; falling edges advance or extend the middle state.
Each state represents every valid phase-shaped subarray ending at the current index, so the final-state maximum is exactly the answer.
editorial: Each state represents every valid phase-shaped subarray ending at the current index, so the final-state maximum is exactly the answer.

tests.explanation: The entire array follows increase, decrease, increase and sums to ten.
The best valid subarray is [-2,-1,-3,0,2], whose sum is negative four.
